title: How a Language Model Works
topic: Language models, reasoning and tool use
tagline: Train a tiny language model, test worked solutions, and explore a tool-using loop.
hub_blurb: Train a tiny transformer, compare arithmetic strategies, and explore a scripted agent loop with real local tools.
card_blurb: Train a tiny transformer and inspect its predictions. Compare direct answers with worked arithmetic, then explore an agent loop with real tools and a clearly labeled scripted policy.
description: **How a Language Model Works** brings three activities into one offline classroom lab. **LLM** trains a real 42,458-parameter character-level transformer and exposes live loss, saved training eras, next-token probabilities, weights and causal attention. **Reasoning** compares direct-answer and worked-addition training, then separates sampling with frozen weights from supervised fine-tuning on checked generated examples. The paired models share core dimensions but differ in context length and training schedule; measurements belong to this bounded experiment. **Agents** uses a visibly scripted action selector with real document search, calculation, notes and context truncation. Learners can choose actions themselves and inspect the exact context available to the policy. The interface distinguishes learned behavior, computed tool results and teaching fixtures, with a Guide, Settings, presenter notes and a canonical printable guide. No runtime AI service or external data is used.
